patch_description:
This crossover keeps the stronger score-aware edge-count size selection from the inspiration program while simplifying and improving the small-graph branch.

For zero/very-low noise and small message counts, it uses non-isomorphic graph codewords and permutation-invariant graph edit-distance decoding. Canonical graph masks are generated directly, and greedy farthest-point selection maximizes separation among selected codewords.

For larger/noisier cases, it uses the edge-count channel. It evaluates all possible vertex counts using a normal approximation of decoding error and chooses the graph size that maximizes the expected score tradeoff between reliability and the score divisor N. Decoding uses the expected noisy edge count.

The implementation avoids the large static canonical-mask table and unnecessary adjacency-matrix conversions while retaining the required interactive protocol and flushes.
